challenges.name: environments-concurrency-quiz
challenges.title: Read the deploy queue
challenges.description: Three statements about what Rice Rocket saw while adding concurrency groups and environments to its workflows. Decide whether each one is true.
hints: Count the slots of one concurrency group: how many runs can be in progress, and how many can wait? What happens to a waiting run when a newer one arrives?
A concurrency group is a string. Which runs share it when it is the constant `ci`, and which share it when it contains `github.ref`?
Look at where `PROD_SSH_KEY` was created (Settings > Environments > production) and at which job declares `environment: production`.

questions.question:
The deploy job got a concurrency group, then three pull requests were merged within two minutes:

```yaml
jobs:
  deploy:
    concurrency:
      group: deploy
      cancel-in-progress: false
```

```text
deploy  #88  main  a1f3c2e  In progress
deploy  #89  main  b7d9e01  Cancelled
  Canceling since a higher priority waiting request for deploy exists
deploy  #90  main  c4e2a9b  Pending
```

Statement: "With `cancel-in-progress: false`, GitHub queues every run of the group, so #89 was cancelled by a bug and should have deployed after #88."
questions.explanation: False. A concurrency group holds at most one running and one pending job. When #90 arrived while #89 was pending, #89 was cancelled and #90 took the pending slot; that is the documented behaviour, not a bug. For deploys of `main` it is what you want: #90 contains every commit of #89, so deploying c4e2a9b right after a1f3c2e skips nothing. `cancel-in-progress: false` only protects the running deploy (#88) from being cut short. The misconception is that a group is a FIFO queue of unlimited length.

questions.question:
The CI workflow cancels outdated runs, but two developers keep losing their checks:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
concurrency:
  group: ci
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

```text
ci  #301  PR #41 feature/momo-pay   Cancelled  (higher priority request for ci)
ci  #302  PR #42 feature/zalo-login In progress
```

Statement: "Setting `cancel-in-progress: false` is the fix: then each pull request gets its own CI run."
questions.explanation: False. The group name `ci` is the same for every run of the workflow, so all pull requests share one slot. With `cancel-in-progress: false` they would queue behind each other, and a waiting run would still be cancelled by the next one. The fix is a group per ref: `group: ci-${{ github.ref }}` (each pull request has its own `refs/pull/<n>/merge`), keeping `cancel-in-progress: true` so a new push to the same pull request cancels only that pull request's outdated run.

questions.question:
`PROD_SSH_KEY` was created as a secret of the environment `production`. A smoke-test job added after the deploy fails:

```yaml
  smoke:
    needs: deploy-production
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - run: ./deploy/smoke.sh
        env:
          SSH_KEY: ${{ secrets.PROD_SSH_KEY }}
```

```text
Run ./deploy/smoke.sh
  SSH_KEY: 
deploy@203.0.113.10: Permission denied (publickey).
```

Statement: "Environment secrets reach only jobs that reference that environment; `smoke` has no `environment: production`, so `secrets.PROD_SSH_KEY` is an empty string there."
questions.explanation: True. Secrets stored on an environment are available only to a job that declares `environment:` with that name, and only after its protection rules pass (reviewer, allowed branch). Any other job gets an empty string, without an error, which is why the log shows `SSH_KEY:` with no value. Either add `environment: production` to `smoke` (it then also waits for its rules) or run the smoke test as steps of `deploy-production`. The misconception is that a secret defined anywhere in the repository settings reaches every job.

challenges.name: staging-production-deploys
challenges.title: Deploy main to staging, then production, one deploy at a time
challenges.description: Rice Rocket's deploy workflow shipped every push to main straight to the VPS. Two merges a minute apart deployed at the same time and the older, slower one finished last, so the old version went live; anyone who merged deployed to production without approval; and a first fix with `cancel-in-progress: true` killed a deploy halfway through its migration. The editor holds `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` with its key blocks missing, each marked by a `# [ ]` line; some pieces are wrong on purpose. The environments already exist in the repository settings: `staging` (secret `STAGING_SSH_KEY`) and `production` (a required reviewer, deployments from main only, secret `PROD_SSH_KEY`). Fill every line so that: `deploy-staging` uses the environment `staging` with the URL `https://staging.ricerocket.vn` and `deploy-production` the environment `production` with `https://ricerocket.vn`; each environment runs one deploy at a time and never cancels a running deploy, so the newest commit ends up live; production starts only after staging succeeded; a manual run from any branch other than main deploys nothing. Run grades the file with a simulator of jobs, environments and concurrency groups on one clock.
hints: Draw the three merges on a timeline: when does each staging deploy start and end with no group, with a shared group, and with `cancel-in-progress: true`? Which commit is live at the end of each?
Look at `environment:` with `name` and `url`, a job-level `concurrency:` with a constant `group` and `cancel-in-progress`, `needs:` between the two deploy jobs, and an `if:` on `github.ref`.

A worker deployed to `eu` then `us`: `deploy-us: { needs: deploy-eu, environment: { name: us, url: https://us.example.com }, concurrency: { group: deploy-us, cancel-in-progress: false } }`, and `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` on `deploy-eu`.

tests.name: Three quick merges: one deploy at a time per environment, the newest commit ends up live
Each deploy job uses its environment and URL, and its SSH key secret reaches it
A failed staging deploy never reaches production
A manual run from a feature branch deploys nothing
Production follows staging; both groups are shared by every commit and never cancel
